name: Body Lock Pass

phases.name: Chest-to-Hip Connection
phases.description: Drive chest into hip, lock hands low around the waist to prevent hip escape.

phases.name: Head Offset
phases.description: Position head to one side to block shoulder crunch and frames.

phases.name: Kill the Hooks
phases.description: Smash butterfly hooks flat with chest pressure before clearing the knee line.

phases.name: Clear Knee Line
phases.description: Step the trapped leg back while maintaining chest-to-hip pressure.

phases.name: Stabilize Side Control
phases.description: Once past, transition to side control pin immediately.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The body lock pass is a hip-centric system — control the hips, and the legs follow. Lock position determines pass success more than upper-body pressure.

decisionTree.action: Drive chest weight through the hooks while keeping head offset — do not release lock until hooks are pinned to the mat.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent is flat on back with no hooks
decisionTree.action: Walk knees out wide, windshield both knees past their hip line, then release lock and pin side control.
Drop chest level lower, drive ear toward their belly button, and walk knees forward to break the frame.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent turns to their side (knee shield)
decisionTree.action: Switch to over-under pass by releasing one side of the lock and pinning the near knee with your shoulder.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent gets underhooks and lifts you
decisionTree.action: Posture up, re-connect chest to hips, and reset the lock — do not fight from a lifted position.

exitStrategies: If passing fails, transition to half guard passing or headquarters control.
If opponent creates too much space, stand and re-engage from a low passing stance.
If body lock is consistently countered, switch to over-under or leg drag passing.

keyCorrections: If stuck, your head is centered — offset it to one side.
If they re-guard, you released the lock too early.
If they shoulder crunch, your chest is too high.
moneyDetails: The head offset is the most underrated detail — it blocks shoulder crunch and hip rotation.
Killing the butterfly hook is not optional; without it, your hips get lifted.
Release the body lock only after the knee line is past and side control is pinned.
safetyNotes: Watch your lower back — do not round it under pressure. Keep hips low to avoid being lifted.
fixItFast: Can't lock the hips? Drop your chest level and walk your knees wider.
Getting lifted? Your chest is too high and the hook is still alive.
Knee line stuck? Windshield your near knee while keeping chest pressure heavy.
description: Use chest-to-hip pressure, head offset, and hip locking to staple the opponent's hips before clearing the knee line. A core no-gi pressure passing system.
shortInstruction: Lock low on the hips, offset the head, kill the hooks, clear the knee line, stabilize the pin.
summary: A core no-gi pressure passing system that neutralizes the hips before clearing the legs.
whyItWorks: Locks both hips before the opponent can re-guard or create frames.
Turns upper-body pressure into lower-body immobility.
Denies butterfly hooks, shoulder crunch, and inside knee pummeling.
Creates a dilemma between getting flattened or giving up the pass.
commonMistakes: Locking too high on the ribs instead of the hips.
Releasing the body lock before the knee line is cleared.
Letting the head sit centered between both hands.
Ignoring the butterfly hook and rushing the knee line.
Standing up too tall, losing chest-to-hip connection.
coachingCues: Low lock, head offset, kill the hook.
Chest to hips, not chest to chest.

oneMinuteMode.goal: Pin the hips and clear the knee line with chest-to-hip pressure.
steps: Connect chest to hips with hands locked low around the waist.
Keep head offset to one side (ear near hip).
Kill the butterfly hook with knee and chest pressure.
Windshield the near knee past the shin frame.
Clear the knee line and stabilize side control.

safetySummary: Avoid driving weight onto the opponent's neck or spine.
Release pressure immediately if your partner taps or shows distress.
Do not crank the neck to force the pass.
nextStep: After stabilizing side control, transition to mount, back control, or submission systems like arm triangle.
